transcript.content: Hello, thank you for coming in. Can you tell me what’s been troubling you and what brings you here today?

I’ve been having a lot of trouble staying focused. I’m a secondary school teacher, and I’ll sit down with a stack of essays to mark or a curriculum document to work through, fully intending to get it done. But after maybe ten minutes, I realize I’ve just been staring at the same page and thinking about three other things, and I’ve barely taken in what’s in front of me. It’s been frustrating enough that I thought I should come talk to someone.
Have you been feeling restless or fidgety while trying to focus, like you can't sit still for very long?
Not really, no. I don’t think I’m especially fidgety or unable to sit still. It’s more that my mind drifts off while I’m sitting there, but physically I’m usually just at my desk.
Have you been feeling down, sad, or losing interest in things you usually enjoy?
I wouldn’t say I’ve been feeling down or sad, no. I still enjoy things when I actually get to them. It’s more frustration with not getting things done than losing interest, I think.
Do you find it hard to stay focused on tasks or activities in other parts of your life, like at home or during conversations, or is this mainly happening while you're working?

It’s mainly noticeable when I’m trying to do work that needs sustained attention. Like with marking essays or reading through a curriculum document, I’ll sit down intending to get through it, and then after a short while I realise I’ve been looking at the same page and my mind’s been off on several other things. I don’t really take in what I’m reading, even though I’m still sitting there trying to work.
Have you noticed that this difficulty with staying focused has been a long-standing issue, going back to when you were a child, or is it something that started more recently?

It’s been there for a long time, I think. Even in primary school, my report cards would say things like “bright but careless” or that I didn’t finish work unless someone was watching me closely. My parents were always finding worksheets crumpled up in my backpack that I’d forgotten to hand in. So it doesn’t feel like something that just started recently.

Do you also find it hard to stay focused on tasks or activities in other parts of your life, like at home when you're trying to read, follow a conversation, or complete chores, or does this mainly happen only when you're at work?

It’s definitely most obvious at work. That’s really what made me come in — I’ll sit down with a stack of essays or a curriculum document, fully meaning to get through it, and then ten minutes later I realise I’ve just been staring at the same page and thinking about three other things. I’m there, but I’m not really taking in what’s in front of me.

Have you ever found yourself acting impulsively without thinking things through, or feeling a need to be constantly moving or restless, even if it’s just tapping your foot or fidgeting with your hands?
Not really, no. I mean, I’ll fidget a bit like anyone does, but I wouldn’t say I’m constantly restless or acting without thinking. That’s not the main issue I’ve noticed.
Have you noticed any problems with staying focused or getting distracted when you're at home, even during simple tasks like reading, watching TV, or following a conversation?

Yes, it happens at home too. If I’m reading something, I can get through a page and then realise I haven’t actually taken any of it in. Same kind of thing as at work — I’ll be looking right at it, but my mind’s gone off in a few different directions.
Looking back, would you say that your difficulty staying focused and being easily distracted has been present in multiple areas of your life, not just school or work, throughout most of your life?

Yes, I think so. Looking back, it wasn’t just work or university. Even in primary school, my report cards would say things like “bright but careless” or that I didn’t finish work unless someone was keeping a close eye on me. My parents would also find worksheets crumpled up in my backpack that I’d completely forgotten to hand in. So, yeah, it does seem like it’s been there for a long time in different settings.

Other candidates (F48.0, F32.0, F06.7) are ruled out due to absence of primary mood symptoms, lack of a major depressive episode, and no evidence of an organic factor or psychotic features.
